title: Wormhole Turbulence
summary: Debug: five R habits that break Python code: = for ==, a missing import name, capitals, a method without (), and counting from 1.
hints: Python reads the whole script first, so a syntax error (the `=` inside the brackets) stops everything before line 1 runs. Comparisons use `==`.
`import pandas` gives the name `pandas`, not `pd`: write `import pandas as pd`. Column names are case-sensitive: `"age"`.
`.mean` without `()` stores the method instead of calling it. And `[1:4]` skips position 0: the top three are `[0:3]` (or `.head(3)`).
